findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.py `_local_labels` / `hop_is_local` accept a provider-block `dispatch_group: local` and treat every silent model entry under it as local (used by the loader's local_voices fallback check and the planner). cheval's `_build_provider_config` populates ModelConfig.dispatch_group only from the model entry, so the provider-block label never reaches `OpenAIAdapter._transport_policy` or `modelinv.hop_locality_of`.
findings.description: The locality label is read from two different places. The loader and planner (`hop_is_local`, `_local_labels`) fall back to the provider block's `dispatch_group`, but cheval builds `ModelConfig.dispatch_group` from `model_data` only. For a provider configured as `dispatch_group: local` at block level with an https RFC1918/loopback endpoint and no `allow_insecure_endpoint` (admitted by `validate_providers` without opt-in), the planner and `validate_local_fallbacks` consider the hop local, but at request time `_transport_policy` returns None: proxy environment variables are honoured (HTTPS_PROXY sends the prompt through an external proxy via CONNECT), urllib follows redirects, no path-prefix check runs, and the MODELINV row records `hop_locality: hosted` for a hop the planner routed as local.
findings.failure_mode: Under `hounfour.locality: local_voices` a prompt the operator believes stays on-host can transit an operator- or environment-supplied proxy, and the audit chain misreports the hop's locality, so the discrepancy is not visible in MODELINV.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve `dispatch_group` once with the provider-block fallback (model entry, else `prov.get("dispatch_group")`) in `_build_provider_config`, and make `modelinv.hop_locality_of` delegate to `endpoint_policy.hop_is_local` so the planner, adapter and audit emitter share one implementation.

findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.py `hop_is_local` is documented as the ONE implementation for MODELINV `hop_locality`, yet `hop_locality_of` reimplements a weaker rule: model-entry label only, no provider-block fallback, no CLI exclusion, no endpoint-host check.
findings.description: `hop_locality_of` returns `local` purely from `entry.get("dispatch_group") == "local"`. It ignores the provider-block label (so a block-level local hop is recorded as `hosted`), and it does not consult the endpoint host or CLI status. When cheval is driven with a hand-built `hounfour` dict (tests, embedding callers, the documented path that `_build_provider_config` only partially re-checks), a model labelled local on a public https endpoint is recorded as `hop_locality: local` with a public `destination.host`. The audit row then asserts a locality the request did not have.
findings.failure_mode: MODELINV locality telemetry can disagree with both the planner's decision and the actual destination, defeating the purpose of FR-8 (proving a prompt stayed local).
findings.suggested_fix: Have `hop_locality_of` call `endpoint_policy.hop_is_local(hounfour, provider, model_id)` and drop the local reimplementation; optionally cross-check `destination.host` against `local_host` and record a mismatch flag.

findings.description: An unrecognised `hounfour.locality` value (e.g. the typo `local_voice`) makes `locality_mode_of` return None and `hop_telemetry` omits `locality_mode` from the MODELINV row entirely. `validate_local_fallbacks` in endpoint_policy.py also only activates on the exact string `local_voices`, so a typo silently disables the local-only fallback check. Nothing in the diff refuses the value at load.
findings.failure_mode: A misspelt data-locality switch fails open to hosted routing with no load-time error and no audit field to reveal it.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate `hounfour.locality` against `LOCALITY_MODES` in `load_config` (raise ConfigError on an unknown value) and, in the emitter, record `locality_mode: "unknown"` or raise rather than dropping the key.

findings.description: Any HTTP 400 whose body contains the substrings `response_format` or `json_schema` anywhere (any field, any case) causes `complete()` to strip the schema and re-send the full prompt. A model server controls this entirely, so a hostile or buggy local endpoint can force the structured-output guarantee off for every call and receive the prompt twice. The downgrade is logged and recorded as `schema_rejected_by_server`, which limits impact, but the enforced-schema contract becomes server-revocable.
findings.failure_mode: Structured-output enforcement for a `structured_json` entry can be disabled by the remote side; downstream consumers that assume enforcement must check `schema_enforced=false` on every row.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the heuristic to the error's `message`/`param` fields and to a specific error type, cap the retry to providers under a TransportPolicy or an explicit per-model `schema_fallback: true`, and fail the call when the catalog entry is marked strict.

findings.description: The path-prefix rule rejects only a literal `/../` or trailing `/..`. Percent-encoded traversal (`%2e%2e/`), `/./` segments and backslashes are not normalised before the prefix comparison. Today the request URL is built by the adapter from the configured endpoint (`f"{endpoint}/responses"`), so no untrusted data reaches this check and the risk is latent.
findings.failure_mode: If a future caller interpolates a model id or other external value into the request path, the D-7.2 path-prefix rule would not stop an encoded escape from the declared endpoint path.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise `r_path` (percent-decode once, collapse `.`/`..` segments via `posixpath.normpath`) before the prefix comparison, and reject any path that still contains an encoded dot segment.

findings.description: An `allow_insecure_endpoint` opt-in admits a plaintext `http://` endpoint on a loopback or RFC1918 host, but nothing requires the provider to be keyless. A provider configured with a real credential (`auth: {env:OPENAI_API_KEY}`) and an http RFC1918 endpoint sends `Authorization: Bearer <key>` in the clear across the LAN on every request and health probe. No warning is emitted at load or in the adapter.
findings.failure_mode: A hosted-provider API key reused for an insecure local gateway is exposed to anyone on the network segment.
findings.suggested_fix: In `validate_providers`, refuse (or at minimum WARN once) when an opted-in http endpoint is combined with a non-keyless auth, and document that an http opt-in is intended for keyless local servers.
